newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opposition joins row with Malaysia, Lee.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opposition joins row with Malaysia, Lee.

text.p: The Singapore opposition Workers' Party (WP) has called on Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew to explain remarks he made in a sworn court statement that have sparked a diplomatic row with Malaysia.
"In the party's view the basis should be clearly spelt out...to avoid any further impairment to relations between the two countries," said a statement from WP Secretary General Joshua Jeyaretnam.

The row erupted on Wednesday when Malaysian newspapers reported Lee's description of Johor state as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings" in an affidavit filed in a Singapore court on January 27.
The affidavit was sworn in relation to a libel action brought by Lee against another WP politician, Tang Liang Hong.

Malaysia's foreign minister asked for a retraction and apology over Lee's comments and its Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday his country felt Lee "should make amends" for his remarks about Johor.
The incident unmasked difficulties in ties between the two countries, Mahathir told reporters in Johor Baru.
"We want to have friendly relations with Singapore. But to have friendly relations with Singapore requires considerable effort sometimes," he said.
The row caused Singapore share prices to fall on Thursday, stockbrokers said, and the WP statement said relations between the two nations could sour if no clarification was given by Lee.

As of mid-afternoon Thursday, Singapore's Ministry of Foreign Affairs had not issued a statement on the matter, although one was expected later in the day. Officials in Lee's office were not immediately available for comment.
